sections.heading: How RCS Reshapes Everyday Customer Conversations

For a brand, that means product cards, short videos and action buttons arrive right inside the customer's default messages app, with nothing new to download and no extra step where a lead can quietly drop off. sections.heading: Protecting Logins and Payments Through RCS OTP Authentication

blocks.html: For secure logins and payment approvals, a branded verification prompt is far easier to trust than a code from a random number — which is why so many teams ask whether RCS business messaging is secure for OTP. It's worth being precise about how that security works: business messages are not end-to-end encrypted the way personal chats in Google Messages are. Their trust comes instead from a verified sender identity and traffic that travels over a secured connection between your business and Google's messaging platform, so a recipient can be confident the code genuinely came from your brand.

sections.heading: Staying DLT and TRAI Compliant on Fallback Sends

blocks.html: Google's agent verification confirms your business identity, but it does not replace India's existing SMS compliance framework. Because most campaigns still fall back to SMS for unsupported devices, that fallback layer stays governed by TRAI's Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) rules — while the rich layer itself relies on Google's verification rather than DLT.

items.q: What is RCS business messaging, and how does it work for customer communication?
items.a: RCS (Rich Communication Services) upgrades standard SMS into a branded, interactive channel. Messages carry your verified name and logo, rich media cards, message carousels and quick reply buttons, and they arrive inside the customer's default messaging app with no separate download. Because it runs over the internet, it supports far richer content and two-way interaction than plain text. Book a free demo to see it on your own campaigns.

items.q: How does a business become a Google verified RCS sender?
items.a: You register a sender agent through Google's Business Messages console with your business details and brand assets, Google reviews and verifies your identity, and you preview your templates in a sandbox before going live. This agent verification process is what places the verified badge next to your name. Ojiva AI manages each of these steps for you.

items.q: How do I integrate the RCS messaging API with my CRM and existing systems?
items.a: A single messaging API sends delivery, read and reply events as webhooks that your CRM, helpdesk or existing systems can consume like any other channel. That keeps every conversation logged next to the customer record instead of in a separate tool, and SMS fallback is handled through the same integration.

items.q: What happens if a customer's device doesn't support RCS?
items.a: The platform automatically falls back to SMS whenever a device or network can't handle rich messages, so the alert still reaches the customer. You get the richer experience where it's available and reliable delivery everywhere else, with no manual switching required.

items.q: Is RCS secure enough for OTPs and payment approvals?
items.a: Yes, for verification use cases. Business messages aren't end-to-end encrypted the way personal chats in Google Messages are; their security comes from a verified sender identity and a secured connection to Google's messaging platform, so recipients can trust the code genuinely came from your brand. Every send is logged for audit, and codes fall back to SMS if a device can't receive the rich message.

items.q: How much does RCS messaging cost for a business?
items.a: Pricing usually combines a platform or API subscription with a per-message fee for rich cards and carousels, plus SMS fallback billed separately and 18% GST. There is no single headline rate — the mix depends on your volume and template types. Ojiva AI shares an actual INR rate card once your expected volume is known.

items.q: How does RCS compare with SMS and WhatsApp for business messaging?
items.a: Against SMS, RCS adds a verified sender, rich media and interactive buttons while still falling back to SMS automatically. Against WhatsApp, RCS reaches customers in their default messaging app on supporting Android devices without a separate app or opt-in list, whereas WhatsApp relies on its own app and template approvals. Many brands run both and let one platform route each message to the right channel.

items.q: Can businesses reach iPhone users with RCS, and how do I get started?
items.a: Recent versions of iOS now support RCS, so iPhone users can increasingly receive these messages, with SMS fallback covering any device that isn't ready yet.
